content: Lansoprazole, when used for a prolonged period or at high doses, may lead to serious allergic reactions. If you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing or wheezing, a racing heart, fever, general malaise, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain, you should stop using lansoprazole and seek immediate medical attention. Precautions: Who Should Not Use Lansoprazole? Individuals allergic to lansoprazole, Prevacid, Prevacid SoluTabs, Prevacid 24HR, other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the specific product should not use lansoprazole. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients in the product. Drug Interactions Lansoprazole should not be taken with certain other medications. Before starting lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. This will help avoid potential interactions. For example, lansoprazole may interact with methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, theophylline, clarithromycin, tacrolimus, certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. Some medications may alter the blood levels of lansoprazole or vice versa. Always discuss your medication history with your healthcare provider. Important Information Before Using Lansoprazole Do not take lansoprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and do not share the medication with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep lansoprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the capsules. Take lansoprazole before meals. Antacids may be used alongside lansoprazole if needed. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Lansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on a tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without mixing it with other foods. If administered through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow your healthcare provider’s instructions. Note that lansoprazole SoluTabs contain phenylalanine, which may be a concern for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). Special Considerations for Children Children under 1 year of age may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider if your child is under 1 year old. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding It is not known if lansoprazole affects pregnancy or harms an unborn baby. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Your provider will advise whether you should take lansoprazole during pregnancy. Do not take lansoprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Storage Instructions Store lansoprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can be exposed to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) for short periods, such as during transportation. Common Side Effects The most common side effects of lansoprazole include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Other side effects not listed here may occur. Contact your healthcare provider if you suspect a side effect. Serious Side Effects Less common but serious side effects include: 1. Kidney Problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis may occur at any time during treatment. If you notice decreased urine output or blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Conditions like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) can occur and may be life-threatening. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes, blisters on the skin or mucous membranes, and red, watery eyes. Stop using lansoprazole and seek emergency help if these symptoms develop. 4. Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS): This multi-organ hypersensitivity reaction can affect the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop the medication and seek immediate medical attention if these occur. 5. Lupus: Lansoprazole may cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Inform your provider if these symptoms develop. 6. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency: Long-term use (3 years or more) may reduce vitamin B-12 absorption, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. Contact your provider if these occur. 7. Hypomagnesemia: Lansoprazole can cause low magnesium levels, which may lead to seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Stop the medication and contact your provider if these occur. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term use or high doses may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults. Overdose If you or someone else has taken too much lansoprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Uses Lansoprazole is used to treat heartburn and conditions caused by excess stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Mechanism of Action Lansoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Dosage Forms Lansoprazole is available as Prevacid, Prevacid 24HR, and generic lansoprazole in the following forms: 15 mg delayed-release oral capsules 30 mg delayed-release oral capsules 15 mg delayed-release orally disintegrating tablets 30 mg delayed-release orally disintegrating tablets
